topics.label: Lecture framing and the cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture’s learning outcomes and introduces the hallmarks as a framework for understanding loss of growth control.

topics.label: Mutational deregulation of growth and survival signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signalling pathways make cancer cells proliferate and survive independently of normal regulatory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how disrupted differentiation changes cancer cell populations and tissue architecture, using blood cancers and intestinal epithelium as examples.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how altered p53 signalling and the balance of mitochondrial apoptotic regulators allow cancer cells to evade death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and cancer cell immortalisation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the telomere-dependent limit on cell division and how cancer cells overcome it by reactivating telomerase.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and summary of mutation-driven hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the account of mutation-driven growth deregulation by explaining p53’s protective responses and then reviewing how mutations generate cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer metabolism is altered and how those alterations can both reflect and reinforce tumour development.

topics.label: The angiogenic switch in tumour growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains why growing tumours require new blood vessels and how the balance of angiogenic signals enables their formation.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and establishment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how cancer cells spread and establish secondary tumours, including the evidence used to detect and explain successful metastasis.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture’s learning goals, emphasises convergence on shared hallmarks, and offers further reading before inviting questions.
